questions.q: What early incident made Coates realize the inherent dangers of being black?
a: A boy brandished a gun at him after school
Being denied a scholarship because of his race
Being stopped by a store clerk for no reason
Being ignored by teachers in class
questions.why: Lesson 1 recounts a boy pointing a gun at Coates, solidifying the danger he faced.

questions.q: Why does Coates describe the American Dream as a “white dream”?
a: It was built on the subjugation of blacks and ignores racial injustice
It only offers financial success to anyone who works hard
It requires U.S. citizenship to pursue
It is based on religious values
questions.why: Lesson 3 explains the Dream depends on the exploitation of blacks and is blind to racism.

questions.q: According to the summary, how does everyday life differ for blacks compared to whites?
a: Blacks live with constant fear of profiling and police brutality
Blacks have better healthcare access than whites
Whites face more unemployment than blacks
Both experience identical treatment
questions.why: Lesson 2 states blacks cannot walk down the street without fear of profiling or police.

questions.q: Which event is cited in the summary as an example of ongoing police brutality?
a: The killing of unarmed Michael Brown
The election of 2020
The release of a new federal law
The opening of a national museum
questions.why: Lesson 2 mentions Michael Brown’s killing as a prominent example.

questions.q: Who is the intended recipient of Coates’s letter in the book?
a: His teenage son
His brother
His professor
The general public
questions.why: The overview says Coates wrote the book as a letter to his teenage son.
